chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Allah the Exalted caused Adam to descend, he began patching [his body] with leaves of Paradise, and the garment that was upon him from the garments of Paradise flew off from him. So he picked up a leaf and covered his nakedness with it. When he descended, the aroma of that leaf remained in India with the vegetation. Thus, the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of Paradise. From there, the perfume is in India, because the south wind fell upon the leaf, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. When the wind stagnated in India, it remained in their trees and their vegetation. The first animal that grazed from that leaf was the musk deer. From there, the musk came to be in the navel of the deer, because the aroma of the vegetation flowed in its body and in its blood, until it gathered in the navel of the deer.
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of musk and perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narrative linking Adam’s physical descent to the material origins of scent, illustrating the Shia concept of the tangible connection between Paradise and Earth. The hadith details how the leaf Adam used to cover his nakedness carried the fragrance of Paradise to India, influencing local flora and fauna, specifically resulting in musk accumulating in the navel of the deer. This account serves as a cosmological explanation for the presence of precious aromatics in the natural world, rooted in the immediate aftermath of the Fall.
